Q1645: The main city of Northern Mindanao, Philippines; the name means 'Cagayan of Gold'.
Known for white-water rafting on the Cagayan de Oro River.
Called the 'City of Golden Friendship'; gateway to Camiguin and Bukidnon.
Q198222: County-level city in Zhejiang under Shaoxing.
Hometown of Xi Shi, one of the Four Beauties of ancient China.
The world's largest freshwater pearl market is at Shanxiahu; also a centre of sock manufacturing (Datang).
Q207030: City in Sichuan between Chengdu and Chongqing.
The 'Ziyang Man' skull, an early modern human fossil, was found here.
Hometown of the Han poet Wang Bao and of Chen Yi, a marshal and foreign minister of China.
Q2304294: Municipality and suburb east of Luanda, Angola.
A big industrial zone with factories and the Luanda Railway.
Founded in 1963; has hosted refugees from the Congo's Katanga region.
Q588: Capital of the Silesian Voivodeship and centre of Poland's largest urban area.
Grew in the 19th century with coal mining and steel; part of Germany (Kattowitz) until 1922.
Its former Katowice mine is now the Silesian Museum; the 'Spodek' arena looks like a flying saucer.
Q200805: Capital of the state of Aguascalientes in central Mexico; the name means 'hot waters'.
Hosts the Feria de San Marcos, one of Mexico's biggest fairs, every spring.
Birthplace of the engraver José Guadalupe Posada, creator of the 'Catrina' skeleton.
A car-making hub with large Nissan plants.
Q320792: The largest city of Equatorial Guinea, on the Atlantic coast of the mainland (Río Muni).
Was the country's capital at times; the official capital is Malabo on Bioko island.
Known for its seafront promenade and nightlife.
Q72990: City in southeastern Shanxi bordering Henan.
A coal-mining centre, known for anthracite and coalbed methane.
The Huangcheng Xiangfu castle of a Qing minister and the Wangmang Mountains are well known.
Q1926941: Town in Bokaro district, Jharkhand, home of the Bokaro Thermal Power Station.
Bokaro Steel City nearby has one of India's largest steel plants, built with Soviet help.
Q29003: City in eastern Heilongjiang on the Songhua River near the Russian border.
Gateway to the Sanjiang Plain, China's 'Great Northern Wilderness' turned farmland.
Home of the Hezhe people, a small fishing minority; Fuyuan, China's easternmost point, is in the prefecture.
Q179665: Capital of West Azerbaijan province in northwestern Iran, near Turkey and Iraq.
Next to Lake Urmia, once the largest lake in the Middle East, which has shrunk dramatically.
Has a long Assyrian and Armenian Christian history; claimed as the birthplace of Zoroaster.
Q571652: City in eastern Guangxi where the Gui and Xun rivers form the Xi River.
A historic river port for trade with Guangzhou.
Famous for turtle jelly (guilinggao) and Liubao dark tea.
Q61434: City on the Penna River in Andhra Pradesh.
Famous for its rice and Nellore cattle (which also became a key breed in Brazil).
Home of the Ranganatha temple and a big aquaculture (shrimp) industry.
Q2485095: The municipality of Culiacán, the most populous in Sinaloa.
Includes the state capital and coastal farmland of the Culiacán valley.
Q2145: Capital of the province of Quebec, on the St. Lawrence River.
Founded by Samuel de Champlain in 1608; one of the oldest European cities in North America.
Old Quebec has the only remaining city walls north of Mexico (World Heritage Site) and the Château Frontenac hotel.
Site of the 1759 Battle of the Plains of Abraham, where Britain won Canada from France; hosts a famous Winter Carnival.
Q2135: Capital of Manitoba where the Red and Assiniboine rivers meet ('The Forks').
Birthplace of the Métis Nation; Louis Riel led the Red River Resistance here.
Gave its name to Winnie-the-Pooh: the bear Winnie was named after Winnipeg.
Home of the Canadian Museum for Human Rights; very cold winters.
Q888418: Town in Fars province, southern Iran.
Capital of Kavar County in a farming region southeast of Shiraz.
Q1624: City in eastern Metro Manila along the Pasig River.
Shares the Ortigas Center business district with Mandaluyong and Quezon City.
Founded in 1573 by Augustinian friars; its cathedral dates from then.
Q170315: Hill city in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, at about 1,250 m.
Founded in 1853 and named after the British officer James Abbott.
Home of the Pakistan Military Academy at Kakul.
Osama bin Laden was killed here by US forces in 2011.
Q198240: Was the centre of the ancient Cai state.
The 1975 Banqiao Dam failure here was one of the deadliest dam disasters in history.
Known for sesame and Chinese medicinal herbs.
Q2656: Capital of Sicily, on the Tyrrhenian Sea.
Founded by the Phoenicians; capital of an Arab emirate and then of the Norman Kingdom of Sicily.
Its Arab-Norman buildings, like the Palatine Chapel and Monreale Cathedral, are a World Heritage Site.
Famous for street food like arancine and for its markets (Ballarò).
Q134509: Port city at the northern (Mediterranean) entrance of the Suez Canal.
Founded in 1859 when the canal was being built; named after Said Pasha.
Has many old houses with grand wooden balconies.
A free-trade zone; its twin town Port Fouad is on the Asian side of the canal.
Q2768828: City in western Uttar Pradesh on the Delhi–Haridwar road.
Called the 'sugar bowl of Uttar Pradesh' for sugar cane and jaggery.
A big jaggery market and paper-making centre.
Q1365433: County-level city in Jiangsu under Taizhou.
Famous for ginkgo trees and nuts.
Known for its chemical industry park on the Yangtze.
Q1011073: County-level city in Liaoning under Anshan.
Home of the Xiliu market, one of China's largest clothing markets.
Birthplace of the warlord Zhang Zuolin; the 1975 earthquake here was the first major quake predicted in time to evacuate.
Q42147: Capital of North Chungcheong Province, South Korea.
The Jikji, the world's oldest surviving book printed with movable metal type (1377), was printed here.
Has the Early Printing Museum and the Sangdang Fortress.
Q568514: County-level city in Shandong under Weifang.
Part of the Great Wall of Qi, older than the Qin Great Wall, starts here.
Known for ginger and green onions.
Q99648: City in the green highlands of Yemen; the capital of Ibb Governorate.
Called the 'fertile province' for its terraced fields and high rainfall.
Jibla, an old capital of Queen Arwa, is nearby.
Q929062: City in northern Punjab, Pakistan, on the Chenab River.
Part of the 'Golden Triangle' of industry with Sialkot and Gujranwala; known for fans and furniture.
Setting of the folk romance of Sohni Mahiwal.
The 1849 Battle of Gujrat ended the Sikh Empire.
Q206116: Industrial district of Kocaeli on the Sea of Marmara, east of Istanbul.
Ancient Libyssa, where Hannibal died in 183 BC; his symbolic tomb is here.
Has 10 industrial parks — one of Turkey's biggest factory zones.
Q203299: City in the Faiyum Oasis southwest of Cairo, one of Egypt's oldest cities.
Famous for the Faiyum mummy portraits of Roman times.
Has old water wheels and Lake Qarun; Wadi El Hitan ('Whale Valley') fossils are a World Heritage Site nearby.
Q17633266: Metro area in Anzoátegui state, Venezuela, joining Barcelona, Puerto La Cruz, Guanta and Lechería.
Barcelona was founded in 1671; Puerto La Cruz is a beach resort and oil-refining port.
Gateway to the Mochima National Park islands.
Q65061424: Greater Malang, the region around the city of Malang in East Java.
A cool highland area with many universities.
Includes Batu, a resort town known for apples and theme parks; gateway to Mount Bromo.
Q622834: A railway junction on the main Delhi–Kolkata line.
Hometown of Nitish Kumar, long-time Chief Minister of Bihar; named after Bakhtiyar Khalji.
Q360326: City in southern Anhui on the Yangtze; the name means 'copper hill'.
Copper has been mined here for over 3,000 years; called 'China's ancient copper capital'.
An asteroid is named after it.
Q496496: City in central Yunnan, south of Kunming.
Famous for tobacco: home of Hongta, one of China's biggest cigarette makers.
Fuxian Lake, one of China's deepest freshwater lakes, is nearby; the Chengjiang fossil site is a World Heritage Site.
Q651101: County-level city in Shandong under Weifang.
Hometown of Mo Yan, winner of the 2012 Nobel Prize in Literature, who set many stories here ('Red Sorghum').
Known for paper-cutting, clay toys and New Year prints (the 'three treasures').
Q760714: Bihar's third city, on the Ganges.
Called the 'Silk City' for its tussar silk.
Near the ruins of Vikramashila, a great Buddhist university of the Pala era.
The river here has a sanctuary for the endangered Ganges river dolphin.
Q1337056: County-level city in Hubei on the Han River, upstream of Wuhan.
Hometown of Pete Lau, founder of OnePlus.
Q63139: The largest city of Cavite, south of Manila.
Grew rapidly as a commuter and university city with industrial parks.
Named after the Spanish governor Pérez Dasmariñas.
Q672672: Former capital of the Kingdom of Onattukara.
Has a large NTPC power plant and is a commercial centre of central Travancore.
Q727731: Coastal town in Kanyakumari district, Tamil Nadu.
Site of the 1741 Battle of Colachel, where Travancore defeated the Dutch East India Company — a rare Asian victory over a European power.
A natural harbour where a new port is planned.
Q221051: Capital of Veracruz state, in the mountains.
The jalapeño pepper is named after the city.
Called the 'Athens of Veracruz' for its university and its excellent Museum of Anthropology with Olmec heads.
Known for coffee grown nearby and frequent mist.
Q1425428: City on the Tyne in North East England.
Grew around a Roman fort on Hadrian's Wall and a castle built in 1080.
A world centre of coal shipping and shipbuilding in the Industrial Revolution ('carrying coals to Newcastle').
Famous for its seven bridges over the Tyne and its football club.
Q19689: Capital of Albania, founded in 1614 by an Ottoman nobleman.
Became capital in 1920; under communism it was closed off; known now for its brightly painted buildings.
Skanderbeg Square and the Bunk'Art museums in Cold War bunkers are landmarks.
Mount Dajti rises east of the city.
Q311272: Municipality of Qatar, part of the Doha metropolitan area.
Hosted several 2022 FIFA World Cup venues, like Education City Stadium.
Includes Education City with branches of many foreign universities.
Q681198: University town in Enugu State, Nigeria.
Home of the University of Nigeria (1960), the first indigenous university in the country.
Near Igbo-Ukwu, where famous 9th-century bronzes were found, and the Opi iron-smelting site.
Q925293: County-level city in Jiangsu under Zhenjiang.
The world's biggest centre of eyeglass lenses: about half of all lenses are made here.
Known for Southern Dynasties royal tomb sculptures (stone qilin).
Q188901: City in São Paulo state, the second-largest outside Greater São Paulo after Campinas.
Grew as a mule-trading fair town on the route south in colonial times.
Today an industrial city with many factories (e.g. Toyota).
Q657428: Historic port city on Somalia's Indian Ocean coast, southwest of Mogadishu.
Capital of the Lower Shabelle region; home of the Bimal clan.
Known for its old coral-stone buildings.
Q42099: City in Gyeonggi Province between Seoul and Incheon.
One of the most densely populated cities in South Korea.
Hosts the Bucheon International Fantastic Film Festival and a comics (manhwa) museum.
Q270041: Yemen's main port on the Red Sea, capital of Hodeidah Governorate.
Most of Yemen's food and fuel imports arrive here.
Was the focus of fierce fighting in the civil war in 2018.
Q269899: City in the Vidarbha region of Maharashtra.
Known for the Ambadevi temple from which its name may come.
A cotton-trading centre; the reformer Sant Gadge Baba worked here.
Q208097: Capital of Manipur in northeast India.
Centre of the Kingdom of Manipur; Kangla Fort was the royal seat.
The 1944 Battles of Imphal and Kohima stopped the Japanese invasion of India.
Has Ima Keithel, one of the largest markets run entirely by women; modern polo developed here.
Q193428: City in Osaka Prefecture, one of Japan's most important medieval ports.
The Daisen Kofun, tomb of Emperor Nintoku, is the largest grave in the world by area (World Heritage Site).
Famous for high-quality knives — once for swords and guns.
Birthplace of tea master Sen no Rikyū.
Q45301: City on Turkey's Black Sea coast; historically Trebizond.
Founded by Greeks in 756 BC; capital of the Byzantine Empire of Trebizond (1204–1461).
The Sumela Monastery clings to a cliff nearby; the Hagia Sophia of Trabzon has Byzantine frescoes.
Known for anchovies (hamsi), hazelnuts and tea.
Q239580: Zambia's second-largest city, in the Copperbelt.
Grew around the Nkana copper mine since the 1930s.
Home of the Copperbelt University and the Nkana football club.
Q1005786: The most densely populated municipality of Luanda, Angola.
A large working-class district of musseques (informal settlements).
Q868203: Capital of Osun State in southwestern Nigeria.
The Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove, a forest of shrines and sculptures to the river goddess Osun, is a World Heritage Site.
The yearly Osun-Osogbo festival draws pilgrims from around the world.
Austrian artist Susanne Wenger helped restore the grove.
Q633036: The largest city of northeastern Thailand (Isan), also called Korat.
Gateway to the Isan region and Khao Yai National Park.
Its heroine Thao Suranari defended the city against Laos in 1826; her statue is the city's centre.
Phimai, a large Khmer temple, is nearby.
